text:
carl_acme: Hey team — getting a big spike of 502s for hosted inference in eu-west-1 starting ~06:10 UTC. Customer traffic shows TLS handshake failures + 502s. Their path: our gateway -> edge -> upstream.

support_annie: Sorry about that, Carl. Can you paste the curl output and any client-side error?

carl_acme: curl -v to api.redwood.example.com returns: 
```
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (52.18.XX.XX) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood.example.com:443 
```
Also seeing 502s in app logs with upstream TLS errors: 
```
[edge] 2026-03-15T06:11:02Z ERROR upstream_ssl_handshake_failed: SSL routines:ssl3_get_server_certificate:certificate verify failed (certificate expired?)
[gateway] 2026-03-15T06:11:02Z WARN upstream_returned_502: upstream error code=502 reason="handshake failed"
```

support_annie: Thx — tagging SRE @sre_lee and runtime eng @eng_jordan. deploy-bot, any deploys/rotations around 06:00-06:15? :eyes:

deploy-bot: [deploy] 2026-03-15T05:57:00Z cert-rotation-job triggered for prod-certs; rollout started 05:58; final commit applied 06:01. No rollbacks.

sre_lee: I'm seeing region-localized failures — only eu-west-1 and a handful of clients in eu-central. Other regions fine. Edge nodes in eu-west show mixed cert chains: some present the new cert, some still serve old chain (expired intermediate). Suspect propagation/caching issue with resolver/CDN routing.

eng_jordan: Could be that an intermediate cert renewal produced a new chain order and some edge caches still have the old bundle. Need to confirm chain presented and what upstream LB verifies. Can you capture s_client output?

carl_acme: Ran these from affected client: 
```
# from customer host
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = ExampleCA, CN = ExampleCA Root
verify error:num=10:certificate has expired
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.redwood.example.com
   i:/CN=ExampleCA Intermediate (issued 2024-02-01)
 1 s:/CN=ExampleCA Intermediate
   i:/CN=ExampleCA Root
---
---
SSL handshake has read 3256 bytes, written 456 bytes
---
```
Notes: client sees expired cert in chain. But hitting different edge IPs sometimes shows correct chain.

sre_lee: OK that matches. Two hypotheses: 1) Some edges still serve cached old chain (expired intermediate) after rotation. 2) DNS resolver or CDN routing sends traffic to an old origin in the pool with stale certs due to DNS caching. Let's check DNS and resolver responses.

support_annie: Carl, can you run `dig +short api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8` and `dig +trace api.redwood.example.com` from the affected client?

carl_acme: Results: 
```
# dig +short @8.8.8.8
52.18.XX.XX
52.18.YY.YY
# dig +trace
; <<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> +trace api.redwood.example.com
.  3600 IN NS a.root-servers.net.
... (truncated) ...
api.redwood.example.com. 300 IN A 52.18.XX.XX
api.redwood.example.com. 300 IN A 52.18.YY.YY
```
TTL on record=300s. However, customer reported TTL 300 earlier but their resolver returned an old CNAME mapping for 900s to an internal edge hostname.

eng_jordan: Hmm, if an upstream CDN/edge hostname CNAME had a longer TTL during rotation, recursive resolvers might have cached an old mapping to a node still with old cert. Need to check our edge hostname records, and whether we rotated certs and flipped CNAME targets.

sre_lee: I'm pulling edge logs for the old backend IP 52.18.XX.XX — seeing last cert update on that node at 05:40 UTC (old cert) and update event at 06:02 for many but not all hosts. Some nodes failed TLS reload due to race with a local cache clear.

support_annie: Action items: 1) SRE to reconcile nodes still serving old chain and force reload/clear. 2) Eng to verify cert bundle ordering and fallback behavior in runtime. 3) Support to coordinate customer and confirm once fixed.

eng_jordan: Quick fix: force config reload + restart TLS worker on the lagging edge nodes. Also push a TTL purge to our CDN DNS and post a short notice to customers. I'll run a selective reload on the residual nodes now.

sre_lee: Reloads initiated for 52.18.XX.XX and a couple others. Monitoring for handshake success.

(2 min later)
sre_lee: Reloads completed on 3 nodes; handshake failures dropped ~70% for the affected customer. Still 1 node left showing expired chain, agent shows reload failed due to file descriptor leak — investigating.

carl_acme: I still see intermittent 502s but reduced. happy to test again when you confirm last node fixed.

eng_jordan: Found root cause: our cert rotation job rotated the leaf and intermediate on a per-node basis but used two formats of the chain. Some nodes accept order [leaf, intermediate, root] and others expected [leaf, intermediate] (with clients doing AIA fetch). During the rollout an old intermediate remained on a minority of nodes, TTL+resolver caching made some clients continue to hit them. Fix: normalize chain files and force reload; add a pre-rollout checker to validate chain ordering.

support_annie: Can you paste the commands you used to validate chain ordering so we can include them in runbook?

eng_jordan: Sure: 
```
# validate served chain from each edge IP
openssl s_client -connect 52.18.XX.XX:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -showcerts | sed -n '/-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----/,/-----END CERTIFICATE-----/p' > /tmp/chain.pem
openssl crl2pkcs7 -nocrl -certfile /tmp/chain.pem | openssl pkcs7 -print_certs -text -noout
# check for intermediate expiry date and ordering
openssl x509 -in /tmp/chain.pem -noout -subject -issuer -dates
```

deploy-bot: [action] purge-cdn-resolver-cache task queued; estimated completion ~2m.

(5 min later)
sre_lee: Last lagging node fixed (reload + cleaned certs). Purge completed. Customer reports no more 502s.

carl_acme: Confirmed — traffic looks normal now, TLS chains ok, no more 502s. Thanks! :tada:

support_annie: Closing loop — summary for postmortem: rotation produced mixed chain formats; a small set of edge nodes served stale/intermediate certs during TTL window and some recursive resolvers served cached mappings to those nodes. Mitigations: add pre-rollout chain validation, unify chain packaging, reduce CNAME TTLs during rotation, and telemetry alert on mismatched chain orders.

eng_jordan: I'll open a follow-up ticket for a pre-deploy validator and add a check in the cert-rotation job.

sre_lee: Adding runbook steps for forced reload + fd leak mitigation.

support_annie: Thanks all. Marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
